## [0.19.1](https://github.com/postalsys/inbox-classic/compare/v0.19.0...v0.19.1) (2026-11-19)
Two fixes for 0.19.0.
### Bug Fixes
* **On Linux, a large folder's list no longer goes blank.** In a folder of more than 800 messages, choosing another folder and coming back, or a sync in the background, could leave the list's rows empty, and a row selected opened nothing. * **On the Mac, the Tools menu now has Message Rules and Encryption Keys, and the Message menu has Create Rule from Message.** They were missing from the menu bar, so rules and keys, such as importing a key you already have, could not be reached there.

## [0.19.0](https://github.com/postalsys/inbox-classic/compare/v0.18.0...v0.19.0) (2026-11-19)
Encrypted mail, attachment previews, 24 more languages, and lists that stay fast in large mailboxes.
### Features
* **Encrypted and signed mail (OpenPGP)**: a bar over a signed or encrypted message says who signed it and whether it was encrypted, and Details names each part and its key. In the compose window, Sign and Encrypt (on the toolbar and in Tools) protect what you send, and a reply to encrypted mail starts encrypted. Tools > Encryption Keys makes, imports, backs up and verifies keys. Your contacts' keys are found on their domain's Web Key Directory, on keys.openpgp.org (a setting turns it off) or in the Autocrypt headers of their mail. Search finds encrypted messages once they are decrypted, and `is:encrypted` and `is:signed` find them by their kind. * **Attachment previews**: pictures and the first pages of PDF files show after the message's text. Inbox Classic draws them itself, as it now does every picture inside a message, so no picture of a sender's is decoded by the web view. A setting on the Reading page of the settings turns them off. * **Open attachments with a double-click**: a strip under the message header lists each file, with Open, Save As and Save All. Files that can run code, such as programs, scripts and Office files with macros, are only saved, never opened. * **24 more languages**: Brazilian and European Portuguese, Bulgarian, Catalan, Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, Finnish, Greek, Hungarian, Italian, Latvian, Lithuanian, Norwegian Bokmål, Polish, Romanian, Russian, Serbian (Latin), Slovak, Slovenian, Swedish, Turkish and Ukrainian, with the whole help in each. * **Move to another computer**: File > Export Settings and Accounts writes one file with the parts you choose: settings, accounts, sign-in apps, contacts, encryption keys, message rules and trusted senders. With a passphrase, the file is encrypted and also carries passwords and private keys. File > Import Settings and Accounts shows what the file holds before anything changes, and Add Mail Account offers it on a new computer. * **All Sent and All Drafts**: with two or more accounts, the folder list shows every account's sent mail and drafts together, under All Inboxes. * **The folder list starts with the Inbox**: with one account, Inbox and Flagged come first and there is no account heading. * **Settings in three pages**, General, Reading and Downloading, with the same groups in the same order on Windows, the Mac and Linux. * **Fast in large mailboxes**: a folder shows the moment you click it, and moves, deletes and marks happen at once while the server catches up. On a mailbox of 229,000 messages, a folder's list loads in under a millisecond. * **AI agents**: * Agents can work with whole conversations and with all the messages of a search at once, answer invitations, set flag colours and manage folders. A draft an agent writes says so when you open it. * Unsubscribing asks you first. * Tools > AI Agents shows what each program read, and Undo Since takes back what one did in a chosen period. * Inbox Classic asks the system which program is connecting, so one program cannot use the access you gave another. * Agents never see the text of encrypted mail.
### Bug Fixes
* Searching Turkish text treats ı as i, and sorting by sender or subject follows every alphabet. * A sync in the background no longer replaces what you just did in the list. * On the Mac, Return, Enter and Esc always answer a question with its safe button, and a compose window comes to the front while the app is in the background. * On Windows, a dialog keeps its focus when it comes back to the front.

## [0.18.0](https://github.com/postalsys/inbox-classic/compare/v0.17.1...v0.18.0) (2026-11-15)
Safer sending, message rules and reading comfort.
### Features
* **Drafts are saved as you write**, a few seconds after you stop typing and every half a minute while you go on. If Inbox Classic or your computer stops unexpectedly, the messages you were writing open again at the next start. * **Undo Send**: a message waits a few seconds before it goes, with a countdown and an Undo button in the status bar, and Edit > Undo takes it back. The wait is 10 seconds by default; choose 5 to 30 seconds, or none, in Options (Settings on the Mac, Preferences on Linux). * **A reminder when a file seems forgotten**: a message that says something is attached, with no file attached, asks before it goes. Only your own text counts, not the quoted message or your signature. * **Message Rules** (Tools > Message Rules) sort new Inbox mail as it arrives: a search in the search box's words, and what to do with what matches (move, mark read, flag, archive, junk, delete, or not notify). Start one from a message (Message > Create Rule from Message) or from a search (Create Rule… on the search bar). The new `list:` search word finds a mailing list's mail. * **Send from another address**: list your aliases in the account's properties, choose one in the compose window's From list, and a reply goes from the address the message was sent to. * **The Flagged folder** at the top of the folder list shows the flagged messages of all your accounts. * **View > Text Size** shows messages and the text you write larger or smaller, with no shortcut keys to change it by accident. * **Messages in dark mode** on the Mac and Linux: when the system is dark, mail as people write it is shown dark too, and so is the editor; newsletters and receipts keep their own design. A setting turns it off.
